significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that EHR-model representations exhibit the stated double dissociation—sequence reversal "flips the internal risk/prognosis signal for directed (progression) pairs but not for order-invariant (comorbidity) pairs"—and that a recovered direction causally controls risk predictions. This combines a form-(iii) relation between pair type and reversal response with a form-(ii) steering claim, fixing expectations across a class of trajectories rather than merely showing that order is decodable; this matters because output-centered resources such as MOTOR and EHRSHOT primarily assess predictive performance without making that internal distinction. It would establish both a behavioral phenomenon and an internal causal mechanism; verified failure of the complete pattern would weigh against a dedicated progression-direction mechanism, although failure of only one conjunct would not uniquely establish symmetric co-occurrence, so the negative branch is less decisive than the positive one despite the distinguishable clause-level outcomes. In the topic-substitution check, the generic question of whether scientific models encode established mechanisms would not earn this score: the directed-versus-comorbidity reversal law and causal risk axis are the claim-specific additions.

reach.justification: The principal handle is the proposed "temporal-reversal robustness" model-selection and auditing criterion, supplemented by the "Directionality-Beyond-Co-occurrence Index" and "Reversal-vs-Comorbidity Causal Asymmetry." It is ex ante when used to screen an EHR model before selection or deployment, leaving auditors and EHR-model developers an action window rather than merely explaining an observed error afterward. After model-specific re-extraction, the conclusion predicts a transferable relation—larger, prognosis-consistent reversal effects for directed progressions than for order-invariant comorbidities—but its asserted scope remains EHR foundation models and clinical trajectory tasks, not architectures, modalities, or scientific models generally. The topic-substitution check lowers no credit here because the reusable predeployment reversal criterion is specific to this claim and would disappear if only the broad scientific-representation topic remained.
